stories.title: Baseline (as is)
stories.what_happened: Nothing has gone wrong yet. This is the plan for the coming year, before any disruption.
stories.what_the_plan_did: It serves 99.50% of demand at a landed cost of €20.33M, moving it in 2,413 truck trips. It clears every governance gate, so it could be released to the factory without anyone signing it off.

stories.title: A supplier goes dark
stories.what_happened: The flavour house that supplies Lemon Flavour Concentrate shuts for 13 weeks, from day 7 to day 98.
stories.what_the_plan_did: It saw the shutdown coming and bought 6,967 L in the week before it (it would normally buy 0 L), bought 0 L while the vendor was shut, and carried on afterwards. Service held at 99.50%.

stories.title: A road closes
stories.what_happened: The road from Breda Bottling to DC Tilburg closes for two weeks, from day 7 to day 21.
stories.what_the_plan_did: It filled DC Tilburg up before the road closed — 26 trucks in the first week, against 7 normally — sent 0 while it was shut, and rebuilt stock afterwards with 74 trucks in the following three weeks, against 37. Service held at 99.50%.

stories.title: A key account's promotion order
stories.what_happened: Noordster Supermarkten, the highest-priority account, places a promotion order for an extra 125k cases of Sparkling Lemonade, due on day 10.
stories.what_the_plan_did: Noordster Supermarkten were filled at 100.0%. Where capacity ran out, lower-priority accounts went short first: Groothandel Brabantse Poort (priority 60) short 2,320 more cases.

stories.title: Electrify two lanes
stories.what_happened: Breda Bottling's own trucks to DC Tilburg and DC Rotterdam switch to battery-electric tractors (CO2 class 5), which pay a fraction of the Dutch truck toll.
stories.what_the_plan_did: The toll on those two lanes falls from €9,258 to €1,802 over the year, and the plan's whole toll from €18k to €11k. Transport emissions by the ISO 14083 method go from 211 to 128 tonnes CO2e. The trucks' own cost is not modelled, so the toll saving is the most this decision could save, not its business case, and the electric emission factor is illustrative.

stories.title: A tariff on imported concentrate
stories.what_happened: From day 49 to the end of the year, an extra 25% import duty applies to Lemon Flavour Concentrate, which the bottling plant buys from the United States, on top of the EU's ordinary 12.8% duty.
stories.what_the_plan_did: It bought 19k L before the duty started, against 4,000 L in the baseline, so almost no concentrate pays the duty (purchases +€2,192). On the baseline the duty would have cost €51k. Carrying the stock is not free, but the landed cost change (+€19k) is inside the €114k the plans are solved to, so this run cannot say how much of the duty buying ahead really saves. Service is 99.50%. The concentrate has no shelf life or storage limit in this demo; a real tariff study would check both, and price another source of supply.

stories.title: The new product takes off
stories.what_happened: Noordster Supermarkten lists Sparkling Lemonade Zero, launched in April, in every store for the summer, and orders 100k cases for mid-May to mid-July. Its forecast rests on 38 weeks of history.
stories.what_the_plan_did: It makes 87k more cases of Sparkling Lemonade Zero over the year. Co-packing does not change (11k cases), and Sparkling Lemonade, which shares the bottling lines, is not touched. Where capacity ran out, lower-priority accounts went short first: Groothandel Molenzicht (priority 60) short 963 more cases; Groothandel Scheldezicht (priority 60) short 63 more cases. Service is 99.51%.

stories.title: A bottling line goes down in summer
stories.what_happened: Breda Bottling's Sparkling Lemonade filling line is out for four weeks, mid-June to mid-July, for a rebuild after a breakdown. The date is known in advance.
stories.what_the_plan_did: Before the line goes down, it builds Sparkling Lemonade ahead: Breda Bottling makes 119k more cases and Oss Foods 46k more, and Puurs Drinks Co-packing (BE) fills 59k cases. While it is down, Oss Foods makes 27k more cases than usual, and stock runs €166k higher on average. Service stays at 99.50% (baseline 99.50%). The year costs €230k more than the baseline.

takeaways.title: A supplier goes dark
takeaways.action: It saw the shutdown coming and bought 6,967 L in the week before it (it would normally buy 0 L), bought 0 L while the vendor was shut, and carried on afterwards.
assumptions: Vendor shut: day 7 to day 98 of the year.
Found out late: the baseline is kept until day 7, then re-planned as an emergency, the best re-plan possible.
Every plan is proven within ±€113,540 of the best possible; a difference inside that is not a finding.
Prices, costs and the rest of the year's demand are the baseline's.
takeaways.message: Acting ahead wins back €5.31M, 100% of the €5.29M hit.
takeaways.case: Found out on day 7, a supplier goes dark costs €5.29M of profit and service falls to 76.16%. Acting ahead wins back €5.31M, 100% of the €5.29M hit.
calc: Profit a year: baseline €25,201,639; found out on day 7 €19,911,950; acted ahead €25,217,790.
Hit of finding out late = baseline − found out late = €25,201,639 − €19,911,950 = €5,289,689.
Won back by acting ahead = acted ahead − found out late = €25,217,790 − €19,911,950 = €5,305,840.
Share won back = €5,305,840 ÷ €5,289,689 = 100.3%: the €16,151 over is inside the ±€113,540, so the page says all of it.
Read against the ±€113,540 the plans are proven to: a finding.
Orders served, by value: baseline 99.50%, found out late 76.16%, acted ahead 99.50%.
